reviewer: Codex registry_acceptance: read-only source metadata and adapter inspection

findings.observation: NIH ontologytype is an array; normalize_record passes the whole array to SOURCE_CATEGORY_MAP instead of each value. 39 currently unclassified primary families contain Animals. ontologytype is a facet/group name, not necessarily an object value; ontologykey and free keywords are also merged into tags, losing their pairing.

candidate_records.title: Black Tailed Prairie Dog Laying on Back

counterexamples: NIH 625 Fried Egg is under Animals/Birds/Food; NIH 622 Egg and 621 Cracked Egg are also not proof of a whole animal.
findings.recommendation: Preserve official ontologykey/ontologytype pairs before defining narrow source-specific classification. Do not flatten Animals and call all 39 scientifically correct animals.

findings.observation: Official category-page names are preserved only as tags. Among the unclassified Reactome families, 54 have Transporter and 31 Compound; these 85 disjoint families have usable molecule-category evidence. 13 arrow and 16 Background remain broad or outside the current scientific taxonomy.
findings.recommendation: Consider an explicit Reactome category-to-molecules mapping after source category provenance is preserved; use it only for broad taxonomy, never to prove a particular receptor/gene or complete object.

findings.observation: 24 unclassified SciDraw families have official category_name bird; titles include bird silhouette, California thrasher and Zebra Finch. One European starling operant conditioning scene shows why category alone is not a view/action guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Consider bird as a broad animals category only. The 23 human-category families include Adrenal gland, so human must not become whole-person evidence.

findings.observation: All 676 unclassified primary Togo families have empty categories/upstream_category. Official other_tags_comma_en and taxon1/2/3_en are merged into tags. 365 have at least one selected animal taxon tag; 59 have Organs; 162 have selected plant tags. These overlap and are not proposed auto-classification counts.
counterexamples: Togo 2111 Harmonia axyridis has contradictory Mammals/Vertebrates and Insecta tags.
Togo 1913 Horse's hoof is an animal part, not the whole horse.
Togo 2195 Polycystic ovary syndrome carries Mammalia/Homo sapiens but depicts an anatomical condition.
Togo Organs contains pelvis, ligaments and vessels, which cross our organs/tissues split.
findings.recommendation: Preserve official taxon hierarchy and subject tags in distinct fields with source evidence. Narrow classification may use them with conflict handling; do not globally map Organisms or Mammalia to primary animal. Plant/generic components may legitimately stay outside the 12 medical buckets.

findings.observation: Unclassified official categories include symbols102, typography47, devices41, specialties24, emotions24. devices contains Ventilator/ECMO but also Toilet Paper, Mobile App and High Temperature; specialties includes clinical services but also Gym and Chaplaincy.
findings.recommendation: Expose official categories independently; map narrow objects when evidence supports them. Do not map all devices to laboratory equipment, all specialties to workflow, or all symbols to omics.

findings.observation: The 821 unclassified primary families are Human_physiology276, General_items175, Blood_Immunology131, Plants_Algae95, Parasites64, Safety_symbols43, Oncology20, Imaging13, Nanotechnology4. These are mixed subject buckets. Examples larynx and venous system are plausible ordinary-vocabulary gaps, MHC2 is a molecular abbreviation, but arrows/sweets/drug tablets cannot all become organs.
findings.recommendation: Keep original subject facets; prioritize specific source object names and narrowly evidenced synonym work, separate from official-category mapping. No broad source bucket should supply a medical principal object.

findings.observation: 35 families retain official common/scientific names and correct style/family metadata. They include Hydrozoan, Tardigrade, Common marmoset, Human, algae and Thale cress. No medical-category field was observed in the current adapter/gallery enrichment.
findings.recommendation: Do not infer animals merely from Arcadia membership. Future taxonomy expansion can use explicit organism taxonomy with evidence; current absence is not a missing download or failed rendering.

findings.observation: The four unclassified items are Axes, Curved Arrow, Layers, Arrow Right under official general-science.
findings.recommendation: Keep them searchable as generic drawing components; do not classify as clinical workflow or experimental action just to make taxonomy counts complete.

limitations: No new image review was performed for this metadata diagnostic.
Unclassified is a taxonomy condition, not failed licensing/acquisition/rendering and not evidence that artwork is irrelevant.
Source subject and organism tags must not silently prove primary object, species, view, state or action.
Scope questions are still pending and this is not the final appearance-bound release catalog.

steps.change: Preserve source subject facets separately from scientific assertions.
steps.suggested_field: source_subject_facets: [{source, kind: official_catalog_category, label, evidence_url, upstream_revision}]
steps.details: At discovery record the actual category-page URL for Reactome; for existing Reactome records, only migrate tags because this adapter writes category labels exclusively, and bind the archived record/adapter provenance without inventing a missing category URL. SciDraw already preserves category_name as upstream_category. Keep broad category metadata visible even when no canonical taxonomy mapping exists.

steps.change: Add only source-scoped canonical topic mappings: Reactome Transporter/Compound -> molecules; SciDraw bird -> animals.
steps.not_an_acceptance_claim: These are counts of metadata candidates for broad topic classification, not 109 new scientific/view matches or visual passes. Existing scope filtering remains authoritative.

steps.change: Add a reusable scalar/list parser for upstream categories with regression tests, but defer NIH Animals classification.
steps.details: NIH ontologytype and ontologykey must be retained as paired official facets; flattening ontologytype alone can mislabel Fried Egg. Do not add NIH topic labels until an explicit mapping/conflict policy is reviewed.

steps.change: Keep source_subject_facets and canonical topic taxonomy out of primary object/species/view/state/role assertions.
steps.details: Topic category filtering may use canonical taxonomy, but scientific hard filters continue requiring direct source object evidence or exact-file visual assertions. Changes to topic results require a new frozen catalog/index and disclosed diagnostic delta; do not rewrite old snapshots.

targeted_regressions_to_add_if_implement: Reactome official Transporter/Compound maps topic=molecules; same text in another source free tag does not activate this source-specific rule.
SciDraw official bird maps topic=animals; human-category Adrenal gland does not become a whole human.
NIH scalar/list categories parse without stringifying the whole list, while Fried Egg remains free of a newly fabricated whole-animal assertion.
New topic labels do not create object/species/view/state/role facts; molecular family does not satisfy a specifically requested named molecule without its own evidence.
Excluded/pending file remains absent from public catalog, search, download and packs even if its subject would otherwise map.
Togo contradictory labels are preserved/disclosed, never resolved by Mammalia tag priority.
no_change_needed_now: No search ranking change is proposed.
